content:
Sportscaster Bob Costas deemed President Donald Trump a “sociopath” who is “grotesquely unfit” for public office before offering a blistering takedown of the Trump administration’s recent actions.

A longtime Trump critic, Costas appeared on the “Next Question with Katie Couric” podcast this week, where he reflected on the eulogy he delivered for late St. Louis Cardinals player Stan Musial.

The 29-time Emmy Award winner alluded to Musial, who died in 2013 at age 92, while offering a detailed condemnation of Trump.

“You cannot have regard for decency, which is what informed my eulogy for Stan Musial, and not, on the other hand, be appalled by someone like Donald Trump, who is clearly and grotesquely unfit intellectually, temperamentally and ethically to hold any position of public trust,” he said. “Some of us saw that from the start. Every single day provides now [a] well past critical mass level of evidence to that effect.”

After deeming the Trump administration “blatantly, almost cartoonishly corrupt,” Costas then called out the president for his history of incendiary comments and social media posts, noting: “If he was your next-door neighbor, that’s when you’d build a wall because that guy’s unhinged.”

Later in the interview, Costas evoked Washington Irving’s famous literary character, Rip Van Winkle, who awakes to a changed world after falling into a deep sleep for 20 years.

As to what he imagined Van Winkle would say if he encountered America’s current political climate for the first time, he quipped: “‘Maybe the president of the United States deserves to be criticized, but that can’t be true. The president of the United States is not a sociopath!’ Yes he is, yes he is.”

Costas, 74, describes himself as a “center-left person” and never shied away from political discourse. In 2025, he blasted ABC News and CBS News for agreeing to cash settlements with Trump after the president sued the media outlets for defamation and news distortion, respectively. Neither outlet was found guilty of any wrongdoing.

“Because he is the president, to a certain extent, who he is and what he does, and what is done in his name, has been normalized so that responsible journalists have to pretend that there’s always two sides to this,” he said at the time. “There really isn’t two sides to much of what Donald Trump represents.”

In his chat with Couric, Costas called out “spineless and shameless” Republicans who have attempted to distance themselves from Trump in recent months, as well as former President Joe Biden, whose “irresponsible” decision to run for a second term ended up holding the Democratic Party “hostage.”

He also urged Democrats not to “take away the wrong message” from this month’s midterm elections, which saw the party take control of both chambers of Congress.

“The public was not embracing everything the Democrats have stood for, or the fecklessness of the Democrats that gave them Donald Trump a second time,” he said.
